claude_only.name: When must a party-to-host link be reified as a Party Role assertion rather than expressed as a direct binary property?
What is the minimal tuple that makes a Party Role assertion well-formed?
Is there a scoping party distinct from the host that defines or acknowledges the role, and how is it recorded?
Which facts are lost when the assertion is projected to a binary shorthand, and is the projection declared lossy?
Which authoritative master-system identifier governs this role assertion, and which body issues it?
What identifier is minted when no authoritative master-system or governed global identifier exists?
Which attribute changes create a new assertion rather than a new version of the existing one?
How are duplicate assertions contributed by multiple systems detected, ranked and merged?
Which axis does this role type express: functional participation, structural competency, contractual position or statutory status?
Which controlled vocabulary and version supplies the role type, and what is the binding strength?
May one assertion carry more than one role type, and how is a multi-typed assertion interpreted?
How is a local or unmapped role term carried without breaking consumers bound to the governed vocabulary?
Who owns the role-type vocabulary and by what process are new terms admitted or rejected?
How are deprecated or superseded terms handled in assertions that already cite them?
What behaviour is required when a consumer encounters a term from a newer vocabulary version than it knows?
Are role terms hierarchical, and does a broader term subsume assertions made with a narrower one?
What kind of host does this role attach to: an object, an activity or event, an agreement, an organization, or another party?
How is the host referenced so the assertion stays resolvable when the host is versioned or re-identified?
May one assertion span multiple hosts, or is a separate assertion required per host?
What happens to the assertion when its host is deleted, merged or superseded?
Does a role asserted on a container host apply to its parts, and is that reach materialised or computed at query time?
Are direct and indirect holdings distinguished, and how is the derivation path recorded?
When a host is derived from or supersedes another, do existing roles carry over automatically?
Which party kinds are admissible players for this role type: natural person, organization, group, automated agent, or an unfilled post?
How is a vacant or not-yet-assigned position represented distinctly from a terminated role?
May a collective such as a team, committee or class of parties hold the role as a single player?
Are automated or AI agents permitted players, and what additional attribution is required when they are?
Which identifier scheme authoritatively identifies the player, and what is the documented fallback order?
How is the assertion kept correct when the player is merged, split or re-identified upstream?
May a player be pseudonymous or identified only by position, and under what conditions?
How often must player identity be re-verified, and what happens if re-verification lapses?
What spatial, jurisdictional or organizational-unit extent narrows this role within its host?
Is a quantitative extent such as a share, quota or threshold part of the role, and in what unit?
Which role-specific characteristics are permitted, and are their names and value types validated?
Do differing qualifiers narrow a single assertion or require separate assertions?
What are the start and end instants of the role period, and how is an open-ended role expressed?
Are period boundaries inclusive or exclusive, and at what precision are they compared?
How is a recurring, rota-based or on-call role period represented without exploding into thousands of assertions?
Which offset is recorded, and is it the offset legally relevant to the host's jurisdiction?
When was the assertion recorded, and how does that differ from when the role took effect?
How is a retroactive correction of an erroneous record distinguished from a genuine change in the role itself?
Can the register answer who held role R on host H as of date D as known on date E?
Which period types beyond the role period are tracked for this assertion?
What is the permitted state set for a role assertion, and which transitions are legal?
Is the registration state of the record kept distinct from the substantive state of the role?
Which reason codes must accompany suspension, revocation and termination?
Does expiry of the validity period change status automatically, or is an explicit transition event required?
Which assertion succeeds which, and is the succession chain recorded explicitly rather than inferred from dates?
Is an overlap or a gap between successive holders permitted for this role type?
How is an acting, interim or deputy holding distinguished from a substantive one?
Who is accountable for acts performed during a coverage gap?
On what basis does this role subsist: statute, contract, appointment, court order or self-declaration?
Which authority conferred the role, and is that authority itself identified and within scope?
Does the role subsist as a matter of fact regardless of registration, or does registration constitute it?
Which jurisdiction's law governs the role, and what applies when jurisdictions conflict?
Which obligations attach automatically to this role type, and are any of them waivable by agreement?
How is a jointly held statutory role and the allocation of duties between holders recorded?
Can factual conduct override a declared role classification, and what triggers reclassification?
Which evidence demonstrates that the obligations attached to the role were discharged?
Who delegated the authority for this holding, and is the delegator itself a recorded role holder?
How deep may a delegation chain go, and is sub-delegation permitted?
How is a delegation revoked, and what is the effect on acts already performed under it?
Must the delegate and the delegator be distinct parties, and how is that enforced?
What may the holder of this role commit the host or scoping party to, and up to what limit?
Is joint or countersigned action required, and what quorum applies?
How are representation limits expressed so a system can check them rather than a human reading prose?
How does representation authority differ from the system permissions granted to the holder?
How many parties may simultaneously hold this role on the same host?
May one party hold the same role on the same host more than once with different qualifiers?
Is this role mandatory for the host, and what validates that it is filled?
How are joint holders' shares or ranks expressed, and must they sum to a declared total?
Which role pairs are mutually exclusive for the same party on the same host, and is the exclusion static or evaluated per transaction?
How is an approved exception to a segregation rule recorded, justified and time-limited?
How are conflicts of interest declared by holders, and who adjudicates them?
What must happen to existing assertions when a new segregation rule is introduced?
Which agent asserted this role assertion, and in what role did that agent act when asserting it?
Which source system, source record and extraction process produced the assertion?
Is the assertion first-party self-declared by the player, second-party from the counterparty, or third-party from an independent source?
Who owns and maintains this role assertion record, and who is permitted to change it?
Which document or credential evidences this role, and is it held or only referenced?
What corroboration level applies to this assertion?
What process must be completed before an asserted role is treated as verified?
Does a licence or qualification held by the player imply this role, or must the role be asserted separately?
What confidence or data-quality measure attaches to this assertion, and how is it computed?
How is a disputed or challenged assertion represented while the dispute remains open?
How is an assertion that was never true distinguished from one that has legitimately ended?
What triggers automatic re-validation or lapse of an unverified assertion?
Which parts of a role assertion may be published, and which are restricted to named recipients?
What is the legal basis for disclosing a natural person's role assertion, and which model holds that basis?
Can the role be disclosed without disclosing the holder's identity?
Which recipients have received this assertion, and is each disclosure itself recorded?
How long must an ended role assertion be retained, and on whose authority is that period set?
When an erasure request is honoured, what tombstone remains so accountability chains do not break?
Is hard deletion of a role assertion ever permitted, and what is the escalation path?
How is a legal hold applied to role history and subsequently released?
Which external construct does this assertion or role type map to, and is the mapping exact, broader, narrower or merely related?
Where an external standard restricts roles to activity associations, how is an object-scoped role expressed without misusing that standard?
Which conflicts between aligned standards are known, and which interpretation prevails in this Dimension?
What evidence supports any claim of conformance to an aligned standard?
Which fields are invariant across every projection, and which exist only within a particular projection?
What canonical serialization is used for hashing and change detection?
How are references expressed so they resolve in both a graph projection and a document or tabular projection?
How is a filtered or partial projection marked so consumers do not treat it as complete?

grok_only.name: What authoritative master-system identifier uniquely identifies this role assignment?
What governed global IRI or UUID/ULID identifies this assignment when no master-system identifier exists?
How is this assignment identifier kept distinct from the player's party identifier and from any validity date?
Which alternate identifiers (national provider-role numbers, registry keys, sameAs IRIs) alias this assignment?
When two assignment records appear to describe the same player-scope-type occupancy, which identifier is canonical?
Must differing locations, contacts or services force split assignment records rather than a merged identity?
May the same player hold multiple concurrent assignment identifiers for different scopes or role types?
What role code, code system, version and display name classify this assignment's function?
Which organisation maintains the code list and is the code required, preferred or example-bound in this Dimension?
Are multiple role codes allowed on one assignment, and if so what is the primary code?
How is a locally defined or unlisted function represented without claiming false conformance to an external list?
Which RoleClass kind (assigned, agent, licensed, other associative) does this assignment instantiate?
Has this record been rejected because it is partitive, ontological or a passive material role?
Is this assignment a functional AssignedEntity role, an EMP employment relationship, or both as separate records?
What named position or performance label further qualifies the coded role?
In which language and script is the role label published, and is there an official translation?
If the label conflicts with the coded function, which value is authoritative for operations?
Which party, agent, device or group is the player of this assignment?
Is the player a person, organisation, software agent, device, group, care-team or other agent class?
Is the player reference resolvable in the adopting Dimension, or only an unambiguous external identifier?
Is this assignment vacant or unnamed, and is vacancy permitted for this role type and scope?
If the player is a device or software agent, what identifies it and under whose organisational scope does it act?
Is the player a group or care-team rather than an individual, and how is individual contribution recorded if needed?
Has a non-actor UN/CEFACT code such as animal-being-investigated been offered, and should it be rejected as out of scope?
What object, activity, process, resource, account or other host is this role scoped to?
Is the scope an activity, a standing organisation, a resource/dataset, a financial component, or another host kind?
If no scope is recorded, is the assignment invalid or is a default Dimension-wide scope authorised?
Which entity scopes, employs, licences or is represented by this role?
Is the scoping organisation different from the player's employer, and is that expected?
Does this role exist on the player's own authority with no scoper, as HL7 allows for clinical research sponsor?
At which locations or spatial extents may this role be exercised?
Which services, specialties or functions are in scope for this assignment?
Which legal or administrative jurisdiction bounds the role, analogous to HL7 territory-of-authority?
Is occupancy of this post exclusive, shared, or limited to a maximum number of concurrent players?
Does this Dimension require exactly one role code per assignment record, contrary to FHIR 0..* codes?
May the same player hold two assignments of the same role type on the same scope at the same time?
What contact channels, endpoints or availability windows belong to this assignment rather than to the player master?
When role-local contact differs from party-master contact, which must operational systems use?
Does a change of telecom or availability require a new assignment record, as FHIR recommends when details are not uniform?
When did this assignment become effective, with seconds and explicit timezone?
When does or did authorisation end, or is the assignment open-ended?
Do planned start/end differ from actual start/end, and which pair governs operations?
When did the lifecycle event (assign, suspend, revoke, handover) actually occur?
When was that event observed or ingested into this Dimension?
If event time is after recorded time or lacks an offset, how is the record invalidated or corrected?
What is the current status of this assignment (pending, active, suspended, expired, revoked, historical)?
If active is false while the period still contains now, which field governs operational authorisation?
Which status transitions are legal, and which require a recorded lifecycle event and authorising agent?
Which assignment does this one succeed, and was there a handover overlap or a gap?
Is this occupant interim, acting, or a locum, and does the incumbent assignment remain active?
When was responsibility handed over, by whom, and what residual duties remain with the predecessor?
Must ended assignments remain visible for a given as-of time, and to which access roles?
Was the assignment revoked for cause, expired by period, or superseded by succession?
Does this historical role remain citable (author, originator, rights holder) after the player can no longer act?
On whose behalf is this player occupying the role, and is that party different from the player?
Who is the ultimate party versus the immediate party in this agency chain?
Is representation direct or indirect, as in UN/CEFACT DEN/DEO, and what instrument authorises it?
What plan, mandate or power-of-attorney, if any, did the agent follow (PROV hadPlan)?
May this assignment legally sign or authenticate acts for the scoper, and for which act classes?
May this assignment issue credentials, privileges or further role assignments?
What value, jurisdiction or subject-matter limits bind the signing or commissioning authority?
Which credentials, licences or qualifications must be valid for this occupancy, and who is the issuing scoper?
If a required credential expires while the assignment period is still open, does occupancy auto-suspend?
Is the player eligible but not occupying, and should eligibility be recorded only on the credential sibling?
Which other assignments of this player are declared incompatible with this occupancy?
Does this assignment violate the who-not-equal-onBehalfOf rule or a local anti-self-dealing rule?
Is a documented exception (Chinese wall, recusal, time-box) in force for an otherwise forbidden pair?
Which permission or policy objects, if any, are derived from this assignment in the access-control sibling?
Does this Dimension forbid treating role occupancy as an implicit access grant?
What purpose-of-use or authorisation context, if any, accompanies this assignment when it is used in an activity?
Who asserted or authorised this assignment, and on whose behalf?
What instrument or source record evidences the assignment?
Is there a provenance-of-provenance bundle for this assignment, and what is its identifier?
Has this assignment been verified, by whom, and at what time?
Which mandatory elements (player or vacancy, scope, role code, period or open-ended flag) are missing?
If the role code is mapped from an external system, what is the mapping confidence and residual mismatch?
Who may read this assignment at bundle, layer, finding and artefact scope?
Is this assignment published in a public point-of-contact or provider directory exception?
Which player or contact fields must be redacted in secondary use?
How long must this assignment and its lifecycle events be retained after end or revocation?
Is physical deletion forbidden while revocation or historical retention is required?
If a player requests erasure, which assignment fields may be redacted without destroying the role-post audit trail?
Which external codes (UN/CEFACT, CI_RoleCode, FHIR, ISO 20022, PROV) are mapped to this assignment, and in which direction?
What semantic conflicts are known for this mapping (for example owner as property versus owner as account party)?
Does this Dimension claim conformance to a named external role list, and what evidence supports that claim?
Is this record a standing assignment or an activity-instance participation, and which sibling holds the other?
If linked to a participation, what participation type (performer, author, enterer, verifier) applies to the activity?
Does this Dimension forbid merging standing occupancy and act-participation into a single undifferentiated role record?

requirements: Resolve every provider-only bundle, layer and finding against primary evidence.
Resolve the model boundary and entry kind before accepting structure.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Record every rejected and deferred node with a reason.
Do not publish while any critical conflict remains unresolved.
